newsitem.title: USA: Diplomat sees Q3 loss of more than $6 mln. [CORRECTED 18:30 GMT 02/12]
newsitem.headline: Diplomat sees Q3 loss of more than $6 mln. [CORRECTED 18:30 GMT 02/12]

text.p: (Company corrects loss in headline and text to $6 mln from $8 mln)
Diplomat Corp said on Wednesday it expects to show a third quarter loss "in excess of" $6 million (corrects).
The loss includes $2.5 million in restructuring costs to cover plans to eliminate several of unprofitable retail lines and downsizing the company's distribution facility.
Diplomat also said it plans to change its fiscal year-end to September 30.
President Sheldon Rose has resigned from all of his positions with the company and Diplomat said it named Jonathan Rosenberg, the former chief operating officer to replace Rose as president.
Howard Katz was appointed as director to fill the Rose's vacancy on the board. The company did not say who might replace Rosenberg as COO.

The company also said a lender has converted about $2.9 million of Diplomat debt into shares of the company's nine percent convertible preferred stock with a liquidation value equal to the amount of the converted debt and voting power equal to 2.9 million shares of the company's common stock.

The preferred stock is also convertible into shares of common stock at 75 percent of the average market value of the common stock for 10 trading days preceding the day of conversion. As part of the consideration for the conversion, and for extending additional loans of $600,000, the company granted the lender 500,000 shares of the Diplomat common stock, the company said.
